crossRefs.note: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
For when a few years have come, I will go the way of no return.
My days are past. My plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.
You sweep them away as they sleep. In the morning they sprout like new grass.
In the morning it sprouts and springs up. By evening, it is withered and dry.
My days are like a long shadow. I have withered like grass.
As for man, his days are like grass. As a flower of the field, so he flourishes.
For the wind passes over it, and it is gone. Its place remembers it no more.
Man is like a breath. His days are like a shadow that passes away.

translations.web: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
translations.bsb: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
